name: maxwell_boltzmann
description: The Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution of molecular speeds (mode speed, m/s) or kinetic energies (mode energy, kJ/mol) in a gas, normalised and computed exactly — never sketched. Choose it for ANY request about molecular speeds, the kinetic theory of gases, why temperature speeds up a reaction, activation energy and the fraction of molecules above it, what a catalyst does to that fraction, or light vs heavy gases. compare adds a second curve (another T, or another gas's molar_mass). ea draws the activation-energy line and shades the share of molecules at or beyond it, written as a percentage (computed from the curve, the same number on either axis); ea_catalyst adds the catalysed barrier and shades the extra share. That share is often too thin to see (a few in a thousand): tail_zoom magnifies the tail beyond Ea as a dashed curve ("×100"). speeds marks the most probable, mean and rms speeds. The axes are scaled for t_range (default 250–600 K), so animating T flattens and shifts the curve on fixed axes — the marquee move ({"animate": {"T": 400}, "duration": 3}); set t_range when T goes beyond it. Paused, the viewer drags a curve sideways (its temperature; on a one-curve figure the pull leaves the original behind and makes a second), drags the Eₐ or catalyst line, and scrubs or types a temperature label; an explore beat naming nothing invites exactly this. Numbers for text: {mb.percent_above}, {mb.fraction_above}, {mb.percent_above_2}, {mb.ratio} (compare ÷ main), {mb.catalyst_ratio}, {mb.v_mp}, {mb.v_mean}, {mb.v_rms}, {mb.T}, {mb.T2}.
interaction: Drag a curve sideways to heat or cool the gas (a second curve peels off to compare); drag the activation-energy line or the catalyst's line.

mode.description: The x axis: molecular speed in m/s (default) or kinetic energy in kJ/mol (the activation-energy lesson's usual axis).

label.description: A short name written before the temperature ("N₂").

compare.description: A second curve in red: {T: 310} for a warmer gas, {molar_mass: 4, label: "He"} for a lighter one.

ea.description: Activation energy, kJ/mol: its line, the share beyond it shaded and written.

ea_catalyst.description: The catalysed activation energy (below ea), kJ/mol: a dashed line and the extra share shaded green.

tail_zoom.description: Magnify the tail beyond Eₐ by this factor (10, 100, 1000 …), drawn dashed with its "×100".

speeds.description: Mark the most probable ("peak"), mean and rms speed of the main curve (energy mode: mp and mean).

show_fraction.description: Write the share beyond Eₐ beside the shading (default true).

t_range.description: [low, high] K the axes are scaled for, and the viewer's bounds (default [250, 600], widened to fit T).

x_max.description: The x axis's end (m/s or kJ/mol). Usually leave unset.

element_ids.axes: the two axes (ticks and captions come with them)
element_ids.x_ticks / x_label / y_label: the x axis's numbers and the captions
element_ids.curve / curve_label: the distribution and its temperature ("300 K")
element_ids.compare_curve / compare_label: the second curve and its temperature
element_ids.ea_line / ea_label: the activation energy's line and its "Eₐ"
element_ids.shade / fraction_label: the share of molecules beyond Eₐ, shaded and written ("4.6 %")
element_ids.compare_shade / compare_fraction_label: the same for the second curve
element_ids.ea_cat_line / ea_cat_label / catalyst_sh: the catalyst's lower barrier and the extra share it lets through
element_ids.tail / compare_tail / zoom_label: the magnified tails past Eₐ and their "×100", with tail_zoom (catalyst_tail, the stretch the catalyst opens, comes with ea_cat_line)
element_ids.title: the title, when set

examples.request: Show the distribution of molecular speeds of nitrogen at room temperature.
Why does raising the temperature speed up a reaction?
How does a catalyst change the fraction of molecules that can react?
Compare the speeds of helium and nitrogen at the same temperature.
